I'm a big fan of the ArmA series. I've played it since ArmA 2, and I've gone back and at least tried the first ArmA and the original Operation Flashpoint (now called ArmA: Cold War Assault).

It's a great game in all the important ways. Absolutely unparalleled in terms of both scope and attention to detail, something that's extremely difficult to do. There really is nothing else like it out there and I'd recommend it to anyone who has an interest in realistic shooters. This is the benchmark for any "military sim" or anything similar.

There is one aspect that has always bothered me and which I feel has consistently let the game down, however. It's not necessarily something you'd notice straightaway, but after a few hundred hours each in Arma 2, Operation Arrowhead, and Arma 3, it really starts to grind on you: The AI is absoloutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awful. Enemy AI can in some cases see through bushes. Hiding and stealth become pretty much totally invalid as tactics or strategies. Friendly AI in vehicles you're crewing are the worst. Sometimes you'll tell them to target that enemy tank that's looking right at you, they'll target it for a second and then turn away and look off 2km into the distance at nothing. Infantry AI don't understand the concept of cover (although in Arma 3 it's much better) and will either stick rigidly to formation or be scattered around, with at least one AI 150 meters behind you for some reason. Enemy AI don't react when you shoot at them and will often just continue to stand around or will crouch out in the open scanning the horizon instead of getting to cover. When they do spot you, they'll headshot you from 800m away or hit your jeep with an unguided RPG from the same distance. It's very difficult to manage friendly AI, get them to go where you want them to, shoot at who you want them to, etc. I get that all this is somewhat inevitable with a game of this scale where the AI needs to be a pilot, an infantry soldier, a tank gunner, driver, and commander, the captain of a ship, special forces, and everything else that ArmA covers, but it really is a glaring issue that Bohemia needs to address and has been very noticably lacking since at least ArmA 2.

With that said, it's my only major complaint with the series. Everything else has been great and Bohemia are great developers who will actually listen to the community and actively help modders, etc. The DLC policy especially is great in a time where it seems every other developer is trying to rip off their community: if you don't have a DLC, you still get all the updates from it, and you can still play on servers that have that DLC and see all the assets, etc., you just can't drive the vehicles, for example, yourself. There is a huge amount of scope for vastly different scenarios and even totally different ways of playing the game - just look at all the Survival and RPG servers, not to mention the insane amount of mods. As such, I still thoroughly recommend the game, and all the other ArmA games. Just please, fix the damn AI Bohemia!
